author: silver state times
title: Lexali Bravo pursues speech pathology to serve older adults and Spanish speakers in Reno
text:
Lexali Bravo, a Reno native and recent graduate of the University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine Speech Pathology and Audiology program, is preparing to continue her education as a master’s student in speech-language pathology at the same institution. Bravo said on June 17 that her career choice was influenced by early exposure to the field during high school and by her relationships with her grandparents.
Bravo described starting her academic journey at Truckee Meadows Community College before transferring to the University of Nevada, Reno. “I am a Reno local who has always looked forward to attending the University. My undergraduate journey began at Truckee Meadows Community College, where I spent three years earning my associate of science degree before transferring to the University of Nevada, Reno. Although I loved my experience at community college, I was excited to continue my education to learn more about my specialty and become involved in the speech clinic,” she said.
Her interest in speech pathology began after discovering Special Books by Special Kids on YouTube during high school. “After doing more research about the field, I quickly realized it was the right one for me. I was inspired by the impact speech-language pathologists have on their clients’ lives and the meaningful connections they build with patients and colleagues,” Bravo said.
Bravo is particularly passionate about working with older adults and hopes to specialize in aphasia therapy for Spanish-speaking seniors. She credits her grandparents as influential figures who motivated her pursuit of a gerontology minor. “While attending the University, I learned about the ways the older adult population is underserved. This motivates me to continue pursuing speech-language pathology and help older adults maintain their voice and ability to communicate,” she said.
Reflecting on challenges faced during her studies, Bravo identified balancing work with academic responsibilities as significant but credited supportive supervisors for helping manage these demands: “He showed me kindness and understanding by working around my academic commitments.”
Looking ahead, Bravo plans to remain in Reno for graduate studies due both to family support and established friendships from her undergraduate cohort: “I feel incredibly lucky to be surrounded by the people I care about most.” She advises future students, “Join a club on campus and get involved with campus life… Go Pack!”
